prompt: Take the square with vertices $(0,0)$, $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, and $(1,1)$. Choose a random point in this square and draw the line segment from it to $(0,0)$. Choose a second random point in this square and draw the line segment from it to $(1,0)$. What is the probability that the two line segments intersect?
Tom is searching for the $6$ books he needs in a random pile of $30$ books. What is the expected number of books he must examine before finding all $6$ books he needs?

Find the minimum number $n$ such that for any coloring of the integers from $1$ to $n$ into two colors, one can find monochromatic $a$, $b$, $c$, and $d$ (not necessarily distinct) such that $a+b+c=d$.
How many subsets of $\{1,2,\dots,10\}$ are there that don't contain $2$ consecutive integers?

Bob, having little else to do, rolls a fair $6$-sided die until the sum of his rolls is greater than or equal to $700$. What is the expected number of rolls needed? Any answer within $.0001$ of the correct answer will be accepted.

Joe has $1729$ randomly oriented and randomly arranged unit cubes, which are initially unpainted. He makes two cubes of sidelengths $9$ and $10$ or of sidelengths $1$ and $12$ (randomly chosen). These cubes are dipped into white paint. Then two more cubes of sidelengths $1$ and $12$ or $9$ and $10$ are formed from the same unit cubes, again randomly oriented and randomly arranged, and dipped into paint. Joe continues this process until every side of every unit cube is painted. After how many times of doing this is the expected number of painted faces closest to half of the total?

solutions.title: Probability that a face survives
solutions.body:
There are $6\cdot1729=10374$ unit faces. The $9,10$ cubes expose $6(81+100)=1086$ faces, the $1,12$ cubes expose $6(1+144)=870$. Because cubes and orientations are random, any particular unit face is exposed with probability $\frac{1086}{10374}$ or $\frac{870}{10374}$ in a round, each with probability $\frac12$, independently over rounds. So it stays unpainted in a round with probability $1-\frac{1086+870}{2\cdot10374}=1-\frac{978}{10374}\approx0.905726$.

After $k$ rounds the expected painted fraction is $1-0.905726^k$: $k=6$: $0.4479$, $k=7$: $0.49999$, $k=8$: $0.5471$. The closest to one half is $k=7$.

**Answer: 7**

prompt: In a $7\times7$ square table, some of the squares are colored black and the others white, such that each white square is adjacent (along an edge) to an edge of the table or to a black square. Find the minimum number of black squares on the table.

solutions.title: Domination of the inner 5 x 5 board
solutions.body:
White squares on the border of the table already touch the edge, so only the $25$ inner squares $(\text{rows }2\text{--}6,\ \text{columns }2\text{--}6)$ must be black or have a black neighbour. A black square dominates at most $5$ inner squares, so at least $5$ are needed; a black border square dominates only one inner square and can be replaced by its inner neighbour, so the question is the domination number of the $5\times5$ grid graph, which is $7$ (an exhaustive search shows $6$ black squares cannot work).

Seven suffice, e.g. (rows and columns $1$ to $7$; $\#$ = black)
$$\begin{array}{ccccccc}.&.&.&.&.&.&.\\.&\#&.&\#&.&.&.\\.&.&.&.&.&\#&.\\.&.&\#&.&.&.&.\\.&.&.&.&\#&.&.\\.&\#&.&.&\#&.&.\\.&.&.&.&.&.&.\end{array}$$

**Answer: 7**

prompt: How many pairs of $2007$-digit numbers $a_1a_2\cdots a_{2007}$ and $b_1b_2\cdots b_{2007}$ are there such that $a_1b_1+a_2b_2+\cdots+a_{2007}b_{2007}$ is even? Express your answer as $a\cdot b^c+d\cdot e^f$ for integers $a,b,c,d,e$, and $f$ with $a\nmid b$ and $d\nmid e$.

solutions.title: Signed count
solutions.body:
Let $\varepsilon_i=+1$ if $a_ib_i$ is even and $-1$ if odd. The number of pairs with an even sum equals $\frac12\left(\text{total}+\sum\prod\varepsilon_i\right)$, and the sum of products factorises over positions.

Position $1$ (digits $1$ to $9$, since the number has exactly $2007$ digits): $81$ pairs, $25$ with both odd, $56$ even: contribution to the signed sum $56-25=31$. Positions $2,\dots,2007$ (digits $0$ to $9$): $100$ pairs, $25$ odd, $75$ even: $75-25=50$.

$$\#=\frac{81\cdot100^{2006}+31\cdot50^{2006}}2=4050\cdot100^{2005}+775\cdot50^{2005}.$$

(Check on $2$-digit numbers: $\frac{8100+1550}{2}=4825$, equal to a direct count.)

**Answer: $4050\cdot100^{2005}+775\cdot50^{2005}$**

prompt: For how many permutations $(a_1,a_2,\dots,a_{2007})$ of the integers from $1$ to $2007$ is there exactly one $i$ between $1$ and $2006$ such that $a_i>a_{i+1}$? Express your answer as $a\cdot b^c+d\cdot e^f$ for integers $a,b,c,d,e$, and $f$ with $a\nmid b$ and $d\nmid e$.

solutions.title: Choose the first block
solutions.body:
A permutation with exactly one descent is two increasing runs: pick the set $S$ of values forming the first run (placed in increasing order) and the remaining values form the second run (increasing). Every subset $S$ gives a permutation, except that the identity arises from every initial segment $S=\{1,\dots,k\}$ ($k=0,\dots,2007$), and these give no descent. All other subsets give exactly one descent and distinct permutations. So the count is $2^{2007}-(2007+1)=2^{2007}-2008$.

**Answer: $2^{2007}-2008$**

prompt:
Pawns are arranged on an $8\times8$ chessboard such that
- Each $2\times1$ or $1\times2$ rectangle has at least $1$ pawn
- Each $7\times1$ or $1\times7$ rectangle has at least $1$ pair of adjacent pawns

What is the minimum number of pawns in such an arrangement?

solutions.title: An arrangement of 37 and a row-by-row search
solutions.body:
The first condition says the empty squares form an independent set (no two adjacent), so at least $32$ pawns are needed; the second condition forces extra adjacent pawn pairs in every row and column window. An exhaustive dynamic programme over the rows (state: the previous row and, for each column, whether an adjacent pair has already occurred in the first $7$ rows and in rows $2$ to $8$) gives the minimum $37$.

An arrangement with $37$ pawns ($P$ = pawn):
$$\begin{array}{cccccccc}.&P&P&.&P&.&P&.\\P&.&P&P&.&P&.&P\\.&P&P&.&P&.&P&.\\P&P&.&P&.&P&P&P\\P&.&P&.&P&P&.&P\\.&P&.&P&P&.&P&.\\P&.&P&P&.&P&.&P\\.&P&P&.&P&.&P&.\end{array}$$
No two empty squares are adjacent and every row and column window of $7$ contains two adjacent pawns (checked by computer).

**Answer: 37**
